newsitem.title: JAPAN: No need for Japan budget for now for economy - EPA.
newsitem.headline: No need for Japan budget for now for economy - EPA.

text.p: Japan's government has no need for now to draft a supplementary budget this fiscal year to stimulate the economy, Economic Planning Agency Minister Shusei Tanaka told a new conference on Friday.
Japan's economy is continuing to recover gradually and it is expected to move on to a private sector demand-led recovery from the one initiated by public demand, Tanaka said.
The government, meanwhile, will carry out structural reforms in the economy such as deregulation in an attempt to rebuild a strong economy in the medium to longer term.
"Against this background at the moment, I don't think it is necessary to draft a supplementary budget as a step to stimulate the economy," Tanaka said.
He added corporate spending is expected to recover steadily, helped by higher corporate profits and housing investments may also stay firm for the time being.
Private consumption is likely to be supported by employment conditions, which show some partial improvement, Tanaka said.
The negative effects from external demand on the economy are likely to decrease due to the correction in the yen's previous strength.
